clue.text: See 13 across
German composer, one replacing south Indian script long ago

indicators.note: replacing tells us one letter of the composer's name is swapped for another

parts.note: Johannes Brahms, the German Romantic composer
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A German composer is swapped out for a figure tied to an ancient script from southern India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one replacing south' means I takes the place of the S at the end of the composer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahmi is the ancient writing system of India from which most later Indic scripts descend.

clue.text: Hornblower producer starts to create series on behalf of blighted trees

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: on behalf of means for, as in acting for someone

indicators.note: blighted means spoilt or damaged, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A creator of a television series seems to be campaigning for the sake of diseased trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blighted' turns TREES into ESTER. The novelist wrote the Horatio Hornblower sea stories, so 'producer' means author, not a TV producer.
explanation.definitionFit: The British novelist wrote the Horatio Hornblower series about a Napoleonic-era naval officer, so he was its creator.

clue.text: Hard escaping from daredevil Hindu revolutionary conqueror's strategy?

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning things over, so the remaining letters are rearranged
escaping from says a letter gets out of the following words, leaving them

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A bold Hindu rebel seems to be fleeing hardship in a tale of conquest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping from' takes the H out of DAREDEVIL HINDU, and 'revolutionary' rearranges the thirteen letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting opponents so they cannot unite is the classic policy of empires and conquerors, attributed to Rome and Philip of Macedon.

clue.text: After game, produced the first card, as the referee did?

indicators.note: After places the second piece behind the first, following the card game

parts.note: whist is a trick-taking card game
to lead in cards is to play the first card of a trick, so led means produced it

explanation.surface: A card player opens a trick after a game, much as a referee blows to start things.
explanation.walkthrough: The referee here blew a whistle; the card-game surface hides that 'produced the first card' is the one verb LED.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee signals with a whistle, so having blown one he whistled.

clue.text: See 13 across
See 15
See 16
Lyricist possibly shows promise with singular British pop group

parts.note: to give your word is to make a promise
The Smiths were a Manchester band; made singular, the name loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A songwriter shows promise alongside a single member of a well-known British band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' turns the band The Smiths into a single member. 'shows' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled user of words is a writer, and a lyricist is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Dirty dual movement at centre of watch?

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters of the previous word shift about
at centre of picks the middle letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A two-part mechanism sits at the heart of a timepiece, though something about it is grubby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like part of the watch theme but rearranges DUAL into ADUL; 'at centre of' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult films and jokes are explicit or smutty, the same euphemistic sense as dirty.

clue.text: Rude type making love twice on grass, perversely

indicators.note: perversely means the wrong way round, so the whole run is read backwards
twice says the letter for love is written two times

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O
hay is dried grass

explanation.surface: A boor makes love twice on the grass in a kinky way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perversely' turns OOHAY around. A yahoo is a lout, after the brutish creatures in Swift's Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse, boorish person, so it fits a rude type.

clue.text: Part of the clique with music man Phil — official

parts.note: to be in is to belong to the fashionable set
Phil Spector, the American record producer

explanation.surface: A member of a clique hangs out with record producer Phil, who is some sort of official.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is an official who examines things, such as tickets or schools.

clue.text: Which might contain noodles destined to be put away in a home?

definitions.text: Which might contain noodles destined to be put away in a home?

parts.words: Which might contain noodles destined to be put away in a home?
parts.note: a meal of noodles collected from a restaurant is eaten (put ...) at home, not in the restaurant

explanation.surface: Something holding soft-headed people who are bound to be committed to an institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noodles' suggests fools and 'put away in a home' committal; really the noodles are food and 'put away' means eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: a carton of food from a Chinese restaurant may hold noodles and is eaten at home.

clue.text: Beano on a grand scale, with society excluded

indicators.note: excluded means a letter is left out of the word before

parts.note: cosmic means vast, on the scale of the universe

explanation.surface: A party on a grand scale is held without high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beano' looks like a party (a British slang sense), but it is the British children's comic The Beano.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beano is a long-running British children's comic, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Deliveryman's ruse: upsetting hair product on journey

indicators.note: upsetting in a down light turns a word over; here it reverses the hair product

parts.note: gel is a styling product for hair
a spin is a short drive or ride

explanation.surface: A delivery driver plays a trick by knocking over some hair gel on his rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'deliveryman' is a cricket bowler, who delivers the ball; leg spin is one of his deceptions.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler delivers the ball, and leg spin is a way of turning it to deceive the batsman.

clue.text: Get moving, have kids (wait until after No 3's spoken about DNA, many-stranded)

indicators.note: spoken says the phrase before it is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: to wait until after number three is to go fourth in line

indicators.note: about here means the letters of the next word are moved around

parts.note: multi-ply yarn has many strands

explanation.surface: An instruction to get going and start a family, with a scientific aside on the many strands of DNA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges DNA. The definition echoes God's command to Noah in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Go forth means set out, and multiply is the biblical word for having offspring.

clue.text: Rounding Horn — about time to get lead navigational aid

indicators.note: Rounding means going around, so the jumbled word encloses a letter
about signals the letters of the previous word are rearranged

parts.note: the lead in a film or play is its star

explanation.surface: A sailor rounding Cape Horn uses the time to find his bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges HORN as NORH, and 'Rounding' puts T inside it. 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris stays fixed above the pole, so sailors have long steered by it.

clue.text: Choral music spot time

parts.note: a mote is a speck or tiny spot

explanation.surface: A choir rehearsal note about finding a slot in the schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short piece of sacred choral music, usually unaccompanied.

clue.text: See 29
See 4
OK if prince tucks into Nuts Pavlova? Not very

indicators.note: tucks into means the royal abbreviation goes inside the jumbled dessert
Nuts means crazy, so the dessert's letters are scrambled
Not says a letter is removed from the dessert

explanation.surface: Is it all right if a prince digs into a nutty pavlova, or not so much?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not very' removes a V from the dessert, 'Nuts' scrambles what is left, and 'tucks into' sounds like eating but places the prince inside. 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving the OK to something is giving it approval; both nouns mean consent.

clue.text: You once interrupted on behalf of Hall

indicators.note: interrupted means one piece breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: on behalf of means for, as in acting for someone
ye is an archaic form of you

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned speech interrupts a speaker representing someone at a meeting hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A foyer is an entrance hall or lobby in a theatre or hotel.

clue.text: Tweet: "Filthy rich and right cheerful"

indicators.note: Filthy suggests something messed up, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

parts.note: up means in good spirits

explanation.surface: A social media post quotes someone calling the wealthy dirty and happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filthy' rearranges RICH as CHIR. The 'Tweet' looks like social media but is birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: A chirrup is the short high call of a small bird, the same as its tweet.

clue.text: After stream his wheels shine

indicators.note: After puts the scrambled word behind the stream

parts.note: a burn is a small stream, a Scottish word

indicators.note: wheels means turns about, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's car, parked by a brook, gets polished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheels' looks like a car but rearranges HIS as ISH. BURN is the Scottish word for a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: To burnish metal is to polish it until it shines; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Keen to make a baby cross (within baby's limits)

indicators.note: within says the cross goes inside the letters around it
limits asks for the first and last letters of the word before it

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
a rood is a crucifix, as in rood screen

explanation.surface: A would-be parent is irritated with the baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but is the rood; 'baby's limits' are B and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A broody hen wants to sit on eggs, and by extension a broody person longs for a child.

clue.text: Flood accepted viral infection is linked to kiss

parts.note: in means fashionable or accepted
flu is influenza, a viral illness
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A doctor warns that a virus can be passed on by kissing.
explanation.definitionFit: An influx is a large inflow of people or things, like a flood.

clue.text: Miles, one with mojo working, roping in rocking Rod Steward

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: roping in means the jumbled charm encloses the jumbled name
working means in operation; here it rearranges the letters of the word before
rocking means swaying, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Miles Davis, his mojo working, recruits rock star Rod Stewart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' and 'rocking' each scramble a word, and 'roping in' puts one inside the other. The surface nods to Rod Stewart and the blues song Got My Mojo Working.
explanation.definitionFit: A major-domo is the chief steward running a large household.

clue.text: "In Memoriam" obsessed groups

indicators.note: In signals the answer sits inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A poem of mourning seems to be fixated on crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the opening of Tennyson's poem title In Memoriam, but it doubles as the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mobs are crowds or gangs, so the plural matches groups.

clue.text: See 4
Bulky contribution to the FT yearbook

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A big piece is written for the Financial Times annual.
explanation.definitionFit: Hefty means heavy and large, the same as bulky.

clue.text: Hairy brute gets even with crossword setter

parts.note: yet can mean even, as in yet more
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A shaggy beast takes revenge on the compiler of a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets even with' reads as revenge, but 'even' alone is YET and 'gets' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the hairy ape-like creature said to live in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Cook the artist's stone?

definitions.meaning: ... Cook was an English painter of comic, plump figures
a precious mineral such as emerald or aquamarine

explanation.surface: Was the painter's work made by cooking a rock?
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl Cook was the British painter's full name, and beryl is a gemstone family including emerald.

clue.text: Journalist involved with nudity presses Democrat to inflict slight aggravation of another's hurt

definitions.text: inflict slight aggravation of another's hurt

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the words around are mixed

explanation.surface: A reporter covering a nudity story leans on a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges JOURNALIST, NUDITY and D together; 'with', 'presses' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means making a bad situation worse with an extra slight to someone already wronged.
